title: SQS queue with short message retention
description: A queue with message_retention_seconds below the 345600 second (4 day) default drops undelivered messages early, losing messages during extended consumer outages.
remediation_fix: Enable data protection. Turn on versioning / point-in-time recovery / automated backups with a retention period ≥ 7 days (30+ for production). Test restores regularly — untested backups are not backups.

title: SQS queue policy grants wildcard actions
description: A queue policy Allow statement that grants "*" or "sqs:*" to a named principal is overprivileged: send, receive, and queue administration collapse into one grant. (Public-principal statements are AEGIS-AWS-344.)
remediation_fix: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

title: SNS subscription without dead-letter queue
description: A subscription with no redrive_policy block drops messages that exhaust delivery retries, silently losing notifications during endpoint outages. (Plaintext HTTP delivery is AEGIS-AWS-426.)
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: KMS key rotation period longer than one year
description: A KMS key with rotation enabled but rotation_period_in_days above 365 keeps the same key material for over a year, lengthening the exposure window of a compromised key. (Rotation disabled entirely is AEGIS-AWS-335.)
remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: KMS key with short deletion window
description: A KMS key with deletion_window_in_days below the 30-day default leaves almost no time to notice and cancel an accidental or malicious key deletion.
remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: KMS key policy allows public principal
description: A KMS key policy Allow statement with Principal "*" grants anonymous key use to the world. Key policies should name specific AWS principals.
remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: KMS key without description
description: A KMS key with no description is unidentifiable in audits and key inventories. Describe the key's purpose and owner.
remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: KMS external key without key material expiry
description: An external KMS key with no valid_to never expires its imported key material, so a compromised external key stays usable indefinitely. Set valid_to to bound the material's lifetime.
remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: KMS key bypasses policy lockout safety check
description: Setting bypass_policy_lockout_safety_check = true disables the guardrail that rejects key policies which would lock every principal, including the account root, out of the key. A bad policy then bricks the key permanently.
remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: EBS default encryption uses AWS-managed key
description: An aws_ebs_default_kms_key explicitly set to alias/aws/ebs keeps default EBS encryption on the AWS-managed key, which the account cannot rotate or control via key policy. Point it at a customer-managed key. (Default encryption disabled is AEGIS-AWS-391.)
remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: Secrets Manager secret using AWS-managed encryption key
description: A secret with kms_key_id explicitly set to alias/aws/secretsmanager encrypts with the AWS-managed key, which the account cannot rotate or control via key policy. Use a customer-managed key. (Missing kms_key_id is AEGIS-AWS-563.)
remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: Secrets Manager rotation interval above 30 days
description: A Secrets Manager rotation interval between 31 and 90 days keeps a compromised credential usable for over a month. Rotate at least monthly. (Intervals above 90 days are AEGIS-AWS-337.)
remediation_fix: Remove the hardcoded secret immediately and rotate it. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store (SecureString) and reference them via data sources. Never commit secrets to version control — scan history with gitleaks if the value was ever committed.

title: Secrets Manager secret without description
description: A secret with no description is unidentifiable in audits and secret inventories. Describe the secret's purpose and owner.
remediation_fix: Remove the hardcoded secret immediately and rotate it. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store (SecureString) and reference them via data sources. Never commit secrets to version control — scan history with gitleaks if the value was ever committed.

remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: SSM StringList parameter stores plaintext secret

remediation_fix: Remove the hardcoded secret immediately and rotate it. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store (SecureString) and reference them via data sources. Never commit secrets to version control — scan history with gitleaks if the value was ever committed.

title: SSM document shared publicly

remediation_fix: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, move the resource into private subnets, and front it with a load balancer or API gateway if external access is required. Verify with `aws ec2 describe-security-groups`.

title: Secrets Manager secret version with weak placeholder secret
description: A secret version whose secret_string is a well-known placeholder ("changeme", "password", ...) is a guessable credential. Only exact placeholder matches are flagged; genuine secret values are never judged. The value itself is never included in findings.
remediation_fix: Remove the hardcoded secret immediately and rotate it. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store (SecureString) and reference them via data sources. Never commit secrets to version control — scan history with gitleaks if the value was ever committed.

title: KMS grant with decrypt and retire-grant operations

title: KMS grant to public grantee principal

remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: Secrets Manager secret policy allows public principal

remediation_fix: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, move the resource into private subnets, and front it with a load balancer or API gateway if external access is required. Verify with `aws ec2 describe-security-groups`.

remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: Secrets Manager secret with zero recovery window

remediation_fix: Remove the hardcoded secret immediately and rotate it. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store (SecureString) and reference them via data sources. Never commit secrets to version control — scan history with gitleaks if the value was ever committed.

title: Bedrock invocation logging without text data delivery
description: A Bedrock model invocation logging configuration whose logging_configurations block omits text_data_delivery captures no prompt/completion text, leaving AI safety incidents without an auditable record. Enable text data delivery to a logging destination.
remediation_fix: Enable audit logging. Turn on CloudTrail (multi-region, log file validation, KMS-encrypted bucket), VPC flow logs, and service access logs. Ship logs to a dedicated, MFA-delete-protected bucket in a security account.

title: Bedrock guardrail without a content policy
description: A Bedrock guardrail with no content_policy_config block cannot filter harmful, hateful or violent model output. Add a content policy with filters tuned to the application's risk profile.
remediation_fix: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

title: SageMaker notebook instance with direct internet access
description: A SageMaker notebook instance with direct_internet_access = "Enabled" can reach the public internet without a VPC, letting training data and credentials exfiltrate directly. Disable direct internet access and route traffic through a VPC.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: SageMaker notebook instance with root access enabled
description: A SageMaker notebook instance with root_access enabled (the provider default) lets users log in as root, bypassing the notebook execution role's least-privilege boundary. Set root_access = "Disabled" unless root shell access is required.
remediation_fix: Enable MFA on the account and restrict root usage. Create individual IAM users or federate via SSO, attach least-privilege policies, and never use root for daily operations.

title: SageMaker endpoint configuration without data capture
description: A SageMaker endpoint configuration with no data_capture_config block records no request/response payloads, leaving model drift, bias and abuse without an auditable trail. Enable data capture to S3 for production endpoints.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: SageMaker domain allowing public internet app access
description: A SageMaker domain with app_network_access_type = "PublicInternetOnly" (the provider default) lets Studio apps reach the public internet directly, bypassing VPC egress controls. Use "VpcOnly" with VPC endpoints for production domains.
remediation_fix: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, move the resource into private subnets, and front it with a load balancer or API gateway if external access is required. Verify with `aws ec2 describe-security-groups`.

title: EventBridge archive with zero-day retention
description: An EventBridge archive with retention_days = 0 keeps events only for the transient default window, leaving no replayable record for incident investigation. Set retention_days to a value matching the organization's audit retention policy.
remediation_fix: Enable data protection. Turn on versioning / point-in-time recovery / automated backups with a retention period ≥ 7 days (30+ for production). Test restores regularly — untested backups are not backups.

title: EventBridge Scheduler schedule without a KMS key
description: An EventBridge Scheduler schedule with no kms_key_arn stores its payload and configuration with an AWS-managed key. Set kms_key_arn to a customer managed key when schedules carry sensitive payloads.
remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: MSK cluster allowing plaintext client-broker traffic
description: An MSK cluster whose encryption_info sets client_broker = "PLAINTEXT" lets clients exchange Kafka records unencrypted, exposing data and SASL credentials to network sniffing. Use TLS_PLAINTEXT or TLS.
remediation_fix: Enforce TLS 1.2+. Replace HTTP listeners with HTTPS, set a modern TLS policy (e.g. `ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06`), and redirect HTTP→HTTPS. Disable weak ciphers and old protocol versions everywhere.

title: MSK cluster without per-topic enhanced monitoring
description: An MSK cluster whose enhanced_monitoring is not PER_TOPIC_PER_BROKER emits only coarse cluster metrics, hiding per-topic anomalies that signal misuse or exfiltration. Enable PER_TOPIC_PER_BROKER monitoring.
remediation_fix: Enable audit logging. Turn on CloudTrail (multi-region, log file validation, KMS-encrypted bucket), VPC flow logs, and service access logs. Ship logs to a dedicated, MFA-delete-protected bucket in a security account.

title: MSK cluster with fewer than three broker nodes
description: An MSK cluster with number_of_broker_nodes below 3 cannot sustain a broker failure without losing partition availability, and single-AZ deployments concentrate blast radius. Run at least three brokers spread across availability zones.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: OpenSearch domain without advanced security options
description: An OpenSearch domain whose advanced_security_options block is absent or disabled runs without fine-grained access control, leaving index data exposed to any caller with network access. Enable advanced security with internal user database or IAM/SAML auth.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: OpenSearch domain without log publishing options
description: An OpenSearch domain with no log_publishing_options block sends no audit, slow-query or error logs to CloudWatch, blinding incident response. Publish AUDIT_LOGS (and slow logs) to CloudWatch Logs.
remediation_fix: Enable audit logging. Turn on CloudTrail (multi-region, log file validation, KMS-encrypted bucket), VPC flow logs, and service access logs. Ship logs to a dedicated, MFA-delete-protected bucket in a security account.

title: Neptune cluster skipping the final snapshot
description: A Neptune cluster with skip_final_snapshot = true destroys all graph data on cluster deletion with no final backup, making accidental or malicious deletion unrecoverable. Keep skip_final_snapshot = false (the default) on production clusters.
remediation_fix: Enable data protection. Turn on versioning / point-in-time recovery / automated backups with a retention period ≥ 7 days (30+ for production). Test restores regularly — untested backups are not backups.

title: Neptune cluster not copying tags to snapshots
description: A Neptune cluster with copy_tags_to_snapshot = false (the default) produces untagged snapshots, breaking cost allocation and data-classification tagging on backups. Set copy_tags_to_snapshot = true.
remediation_fix: Enable data protection. Turn on versioning / point-in-time recovery / automated backups with a retention period ≥ 7 days (30+ for production). Test restores regularly — untested backups are not backups.

title: DocumentDB cluster without deletion protection
description: A DocumentDB cluster with deletion_protection = false (the default) can be destroyed by a single API call or a mistaken terraform destroy. Set deletion_protection = true on production clusters.

title: App Runner service without encryption configuration
description: An App Runner service with no encryption_configuration block encrypts stored data with an AWS-managed key instead of a customer managed key. Add encryption_configuration with a customer KMS key.
remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: App Runner service with root-path health check
description: An App Runner service whose health_check path is "/" treats a bare 200 from the web root as healthy, which can mask a broken application behind a static page. Point the health check at a dedicated readiness endpoint.
remediation_fix: Enable MFA on the account and restrict root usage. Create individual IAM users or federate via SSO, attach least-privilege policies, and never use root for daily operations.

title: Batch job definition running privileged containers
description: A Batch job definition whose container_properties enables privileged mode grants the job container full host access, letting a compromised workload escape to the compute environment. Remove privileged mode unless the job genuinely needs it.
remediation_fix: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

title: Glue security configuration without encryption configuration
description: A Glue security configuration with no encryption_configuration block leaves Glue data catalog, job bookmarks and S3 data encrypted only with AWS-managed keys. Add encryption_configuration with customer KMS keys for catalog, job and S3 encryption.
remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: Athena workgroup without SSE-KMS query result encryption
description: An Athena workgroup whose result encryption_option is not SSE_KMS (SSE_S3 or CSE_KMS are the common gaps) stores query results in S3 without a customer managed key, forfeiting key-policy control over potentially sensitive result sets. Use SSE_KMS with a customer managed key.
remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: Athena workgroup not enforcing workgroup configuration
description: An Athena workgroup with enforce_workgroup_configuration = false lets clients override the workgroup's output location and encryption settings per query, bypassing the guarded result bucket. Set enforce_workgroup_configuration = true.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Kinesis stream without shard-level metrics
description: A Kinesis stream with no shard_level_metrics configured emits only aggregate stream metrics, hiding per-shard hot partitions and anomalous throughput that signal abuse. Enable shard-level metrics such as IncomingBytes and OutgoingRecords.
remediation_fix: Enable audit logging. Turn on CloudTrail (multi-region, log file validation, KMS-encrypted bucket), VPC flow logs, and service access logs. Ship logs to a dedicated, MFA-delete-protected bucket in a security account.

title: Firehose delivery stream without server-side encryption
description: A Firehose delivery stream with no server_side_encryption block writes destination data without a customer managed key. Add server_side_encryption with a customer KMS key.
remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: Timestream scheduled query error reports without SSE-KMS

remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: CloudFront distribution using legacy origin access identity

remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: CloudFront distribution without a response headers policy
description: A CloudFront distribution with no response_headers_policy_id serves responses without hardened security headers (HSTS, frame-options, content-type options). Attach a response headers policy such as the managed SecurityHeadersPolicy.

title: CloudFront distribution on the all-edge price class

remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: CloudFront distribution left in staging mode
description: A CloudFront distribution with staging = true is a continuous deployment test distribution that may bypass production WAF and logging controls. Promote it to a production distribution or remove it.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: API Gateway v2 API with wildcard CORS origins

remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

remediation_fix: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

title: Route 53 zone with force_destroy enabled

title: Backup vault lock with short minimum retention

remediation_fix: Enable data protection. Turn on versioning / point-in-time recovery / automated backups with a retention period ≥ 7 days (30+ for production). Test restores regularly — untested backups are not backups.

remediation_fix: Enable data protection. Turn on versioning / point-in-time recovery / automated backups with a retention period ≥ 7 days (30+ for production). Test restores regularly — untested backups are not backups.

title: Organization without the ALL feature set

remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: ACM certificate with certificate transparency logging disabled
description: An ACM certificate whose options set certificate_transparency_logging_preference = "DISABLED" is issued without public Certificate Transparency logs, removing a detection control for mis-issued certificates. Keep transparency logging enabled.
remediation_fix: Enable audit logging. Turn on CloudTrail (multi-region, log file validation, KMS-encrypted bucket), VPC flow logs, and service access logs. Ship logs to a dedicated, MFA-delete-protected bucket in a security account.

description: A load balancer target group with protocol = "HTTP" forwards traffic to targets unencrypted inside the VPC, exposing request data and credentials to network sniffing. Use HTTPS with valid target certificates.

title: Load balancer target group with plaintext HTTP health checks
description: A load balancer target group whose health_check protocol is "HTTP" probes targets over plaintext, and health-check endpoints may leak internal status details. Prefer HTTPS health checks where targets support TLS.
remediation_fix: Enforce TLS 1.2+. Replace HTTP listeners with HTTPS, set a modern TLS policy (e.g. `ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06`), and redirect HTTP→HTTPS. Disable weak ciphers and old protocol versions everywhere.

description: An ALB listener whose ssl_policy references a 2016-era or TLS-1-0 policy negotiates weak ciphers and obsolete TLS versions. Use a current ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13 policy.

title: Front Door backend pool with weak minimum TLS

title: Service runs privileged
description: privileged: true disables all container isolation: the service gets every capability and full device access, so a compromise is a host compromise. Grant only the capabilities the service needs via cap_add.
remediation_fix: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

title: Dangerous Linux capability granted
description: The granted capability breaks container isolation: ALL grants everything, SYS_ADMIN is near-root, NET_ADMIN can reconfigure host networking, SYS_PTRACE can inspect host processes, and DAC_OVERRIDE bypasses file permissions. Grant only the minimal capabilities required.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Service shares host namespaces
description: network_mode: host (or pid: host) drops network/process isolation: the service sees host interfaces and processes, bypassing network policies. Use explicit port publishing and keep the default namespaces.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Docker socket mounted into service
description: Mounting the Docker socket gives the service full control of the daemon: it can start privileged containers and escape to the host trivially. Use the socket only in dedicated, audited tooling with a read-only proxy.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Sensitive host path mounted
description: Mounting host system paths exposes host configuration, credentials, or the whole filesystem to the service. Mount only dedicated data directories, read-only where possible.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Secret in service environment
description: Literal secrets in the compose file are committed to version control and visible to anyone who can read the file or inspect the service. Reference secrets from a secrets manager or an env_file outside version control.
remediation_fix: Remove the hardcoded secret immediately and rotate it. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store (SecureString) and reference them via data sources. Never commit secrets to version control — scan history with gitleaks if the value was ever committed.

title: Service runs as root
description: Without a user: directive the service runs as root; a container breakout then yields host root. Run as a non-root UID/GID.
remediation_fix: Enable MFA on the account and restrict root usage. Create individual IAM users or federate via SSO, attach least-privilege policies, and never use root for daily operations.

title: Service image uses :latest tag
description: Pinning :latest (or omitting the tag) makes deploys non-reproducible and can silently pull a new, vulnerable image. Pin an explicit version tag or digest.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Base image uses :latest tag
description: Pinning :latest (or omitting the tag, which implies :latest) makes builds non-reproducible and can silently pull a new, vulnerable image. Pin an explicit version tag or digest.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Container runs as root
description: Without a USER directive the container runs as root; an explicit USER root (or 0) is the same risk. A container breakout then yields host root. Switch to a non-root user.
remediation_fix: Enable MFA on the account and restrict root usage. Create individual IAM users or federate via SSO, attach least-privilege policies, and never use root for daily operations.

title: Secret in ENV directive
description: ENV values are baked into the image layers and visible to anyone who can pull the image (docker history, inspect). Inject secrets at runtime instead. The secret value is never shown in findings.
remediation_fix: Remove the hardcoded secret immediately and rotate it. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store (SecureString) and reference them via data sources. Never commit secrets to version control — scan history with gitleaks if the value was ever committed.

title: ADD used instead of COPY
description: ADD fetches remote URLs and auto-extracts archives, which can pull untrusted content into the image. Prefer COPY for local files.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: No HEALTHCHECK directive
description: Without a HEALTHCHECK the orchestrator cannot tell a wedged container from a healthy one, delaying restarts and hiding compromise-induced hangs.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: SSH port exposed
description: EXPOSE 22 suggests SSH runs inside the container. Containers should be immutable and managed via the orchestrator, not SSH; an SSH daemon widens the attack surface.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: apt-get install without --no-install-recommends
description: Installing recommended packages bloats the image with unneeded software, enlarging the attack surface. Pass --no-install-recommends to apt-get install.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: apt-get update without cache cleanup
description: apt-get update leaves package lists in the image layer. Remove /var/lib/apt/lists/* in the same RUN to keep layers lean.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: sudo used in build
description: RUN executes as root by default, so sudo is unnecessary; its presence suggests confused privilege boundaries or a copied snippet. Drop sudo and rely on USER instead.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Base image from untrusted registry
description: Only official Docker Hub library images are trusted by default. Images from other registries or namespaces have unknown provenance and may carry backdoors. Prefer official images or pin digests from registries you control.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Secret in ARG default value
description: ARG defaults with secret-looking names are baked into the build cache and image history (docker history shows them). Pass secrets with BuildKit --secret mounts and multi-stage builds so they never land in a layer.
remediation_fix: Remove the hardcoded secret immediately and rotate it. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store (SecureString) and reference them via data sources. Never commit secrets to version control — scan history with gitleaks if the value was ever committed.

title: Remote script piped to shell
description: Piping curl/wget output straight into sh or bash executes remote code with no integrity check: a compromised server or MITM owns the build. Download the file, verify a checksum or signature, then execute it.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: chown in RUN instead of COPY --chown
description: Running chown in a separate RUN duplicates every affected file into a new layer, bloating the image. Use COPY --chown to set ownership at copy time.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Overly permissive chmod in build
description: chmod 777 (or a+rwx) makes files world-writable: any compromised process in the container can modify them. Grant the least privilege the application needs.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: No WORKDIR directive
description: Without WORKDIR the build and the container run from /, so relative paths and stray files land in the filesystem root. Set an explicit WORKDIR for the application.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Deprecated MAINTAINER instruction
description: MAINTAINER is deprecated and ignored by modern tooling. Use LABEL maintainer=... or org.opencontainers.image.authors instead.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: No maintainer label
description: Images without ownership metadata are harder to triage when a vulnerability is found. Add LABEL maintainer= or org.opencontainers.image.authors.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: No STOPSIGNAL directive
description: Without STOPSIGNAL the container gets SIGTERM, which apps that only handle SIGINT (or expect another signal) ignore until the orchestrator SIGKILLs them, risking data loss. Declare the signal your app handles for graceful shutdown.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: ONBUILD triggers present
description: ONBUILD instructions execute implicitly in every downstream image, running code the downstream author never reviewed. Prefer explicit build steps in the child Dockerfile.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: VOLUME declared in image
description: VOLUME creates anonymous volumes at runtime that outlive the container and silently persist data (and discard later image changes to that path). Declare volumes at deploy time instead of baking them into the image.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Sensitive file copied into image
description: COPYing VCS metadata, dotenv files, or private keys bakes them into image layers where anyone with the image can read them. Exclude them with .dockerignore and never COPY secrets.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: COPY of entire build context
description: COPY . ships the whole build context into the image, often including credentials, VCS history, and dev tooling. Copy only what the app needs and gate the context with .dockerignore.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: SHELL without pipefail
description: Without pipefail a failing command in a pipeline is masked by the exit status of the last command, so broken builds look green. Add -o pipefail to SHELL (e.g. SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-o", "pipefail", "-c"]).
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: CMD/ENTRYPOINT in shell form
description: Shell-form CMD/ENTRYPOINT runs under /bin/sh -c, so signals don't reach the app (PID 1 is the shell) and graceful shutdown breaks. Use the exec form: CMD ["app", "--flag"].
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Build toolchain shipped in final image
description: The final image is built FROM a compiler/toolchain image with no multi-stage split, so compilers, package managers, and build caches ship to production. Use a multi-stage build and COPY only the artifact into a minimal runtime image.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Full OS base image
description: Full Linux distributions carry hundreds of packages the app never uses, each a potential CVE. Prefer minimal bases (distroless, Chainguard, Alpine, or -slim variants).
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Base image uses floating major-only tag
description: Tags like python:3 or node:20 float across minor and patch releases, so rebuilds silently change the runtime. Pin the full version (e.g. python:3.12.1) or a digest.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Privileged port exposed
description: Binding a port below 1024 requires root (or CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE) at runtime, which conflicts with running as a non-root user. Expose only unprivileged ports (or the standard 80/443) and remap at deploy time.
remediation_fix: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

title: apt-get install without pinned versions
description: Unpinned apt packages float across rebuilds, making images non-reproducible and silently pulling new versions. Pin versions: apt-get install pkg=1.2.3.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: apk add without --no-cache

remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: yum/dnf install without cache cleanup

remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: pip install without --no-cache-dir
description: pip caches downloaded wheels in ~/.cache/pip, bloating the image layer. Pass --no-cache-dir to pip install.

title: apt-get upgrade in image build
description: apt-get upgrade pulls whatever is newest at build time, making images non-reproducible and bloating layers. Base images already carry security updates; pin what you install instead of upgrading everything.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Credentials embedded in RUN layer
description: Credentials baked into a RUN command persist in the image layer and build cache, readable via docker history or layer inspection. Inject secrets at runtime or via BuildKit --secret mounts in a multi-stage build. Values are never shown.
remediation_fix: Remove the hardcoded secret immediately and rotate it. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store (SecureString) and reference them via data sources. Never commit secrets to version control — scan history with gitleaks if the value was ever committed.

title: ADD fetches remote URL
description: ADD with a remote URL downloads at build time with no integrity verification, and the layer is never invalidated properly. Use curl/wget with a checksum verification followed by COPY instead.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: GCS bucket publicly readable via IAM
description: A bucket IAM binding/member granting objectViewer or admin to allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers exposes bucket data to the internet.
remediation_fix:
Remove `allUsers` / `allAuthenticatedUsers` from the bucket IAM policy. Grant
`roles/storage.objectViewer` only to specific service accounts or groups:
resource "google_storage_bucket_iam_member" "viewer" {
  bucket = google_storage_bucket.this.name
  role   = "roles/storage.objectViewer"
  member = "serviceAccount:app@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
}

title: Firewall rule open to the world
description: A compute firewall with source_ranges containing 0.0.0.0/0 and an allow block permits traffic from the entire internet.
remediation_fix: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, move the resource into private subnets, and front it with a load balancer or API gateway if external access is required. Verify with `aws ec2 describe-security-groups`.

title: Cloud SQL instance without automated backups
description: Cloud SQL instances should enable automated backups via settings.backup_configuration.enabled for point-in-time recovery.
remediation_fix: Enable data protection. Turn on versioning / point-in-time recovery / automated backups with a retention period ≥ 7 days (30+ for production). Test restores regularly — untested backups are not backups.

title: Container running as privileged
description: A privileged container has full access to the host, bypassing almost all isolation. Privilege is almost never required for application containers.
remediation_fix:
Drop privileged mode. Remove `securityContext.privileged: true` and use the
minimum Linux capabilities the container needs:
securityContext:
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  runAsNonRoot: true
  capabilities:
    drop: ["ALL"]
Enforce with Pod Security Standards (restricted) or Kyverno/OPA policies.

title: Container running as root user
description: Containers should run as a non-root user. An explicit runAsNonRoot: false or runAsUser: 0 keeps the container root, magnifying the impact of a container escape.
remediation_fix: Enable MFA on the account and restrict root usage. Create individual IAM users or federate via SSO, attach least-privilege policies, and never use root for daily operations.

title: Container allows privilege escalation
description: allowPrivilegeEscalation: true lets a process gain more privileges than its parent, typically via setuid binaries. It should be false unless the workload genuinely needs it.
remediation_fix: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

title: Pod securityContext explicitly allows root
description: A pod-level securityContext with runAsNonRoot: false forces every container in the pod to run as root unless overridden. Set runAsNonRoot: true at the pod level.
remediation_fix: Enable MFA on the account and restrict root usage. Create individual IAM users or federate via SSO, attach least-privilege policies, and never use root for daily operations.

title: Container with writable root filesystem
description: A container with readOnlyRootFilesystem: false can modify its root filesystem at runtime, aiding persistence after compromise. Set readOnlyRootFilesystem: true and use volumes for writable paths.

title: Pod with hostNetwork enabled

title: Service account token automounted

title: Pod with hostPath volume
description: A hostPath volume exposes node filesystem paths to the pod, enabling host file access or escape. Prefer PersistentVolumes or avoid host access entirely.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Container image uses latest tag

title: Container with imagePullPolicy Never
description: imagePullPolicy: Never means the kubelet never pulls the image, silently running whatever is cached on the node — possibly stale or tampered. Use Always (or IfNotPresent with pinned tags).
remediation_fix: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

title: Container without liveness probe

title: Pod shares process namespace
description: shareProcessNamespace: true lets containers see and signal each other's processes, weakening isolation between sidecars. Keep it disabled unless containers must share signals.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Pod securityContext runs as UID 0
description: A pod-level securityContext with runAsUser: 0 runs every container as root unless overridden. Set runAsUser to a non-zero UID at the pod level.

title: Service exposed externally
description: A Service of type LoadBalancer or NodePort exposes the workload beyond the cluster. Prefer ClusterIP with an Ingress that terminates TLS, and document intentional exposures.

title: Ingress without TLS

remediation_fix: Enforce TLS 1.2+. Replace HTTP listeners with HTTPS, set a modern TLS policy (e.g. `ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06`), and redirect HTTP→HTTPS. Disable weak ciphers and old protocol versions everywhere.

title: RBAC role with wildcard permissions
description: A Role or ClusterRole rule with verbs ["*"] or resources ["*"] grants unrestricted API access, equivalent to cluster-admin for its scope. Enumerate the verbs and resources actually needed.
remediation_fix: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

title: Binding grants cluster-admin
description: A RoleBinding or ClusterRoleBinding whose roleRef points at cluster-admin grants full cluster control to its subjects. Bind least-privilege roles instead and audit cluster-admin bindings.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Container with interactive stdin/tty
description: A container with both stdin: true and tty: true is configured for interactive debugging sessions, which should not ship to production. Remove stdin/tty from workload manifests.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: ConfigMap holds sensitive values
description: A ConfigMap with data keys like password, token or secret stores credentials in plain text, readable by anyone with ConfigMap read access. Move secrets to a Secret (ideally external secrets management).
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Object Storage bucket without KMS encryption
description: oci_objectstorage_bucket without kms_key_id relies on Oracle-managed encryption keys. Assign a customer-managed Vault key so you control key rotation and revocation.
remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: Object Storage bucket with public access
description: oci_objectstorage_bucket with access_type ObjectRead or ObjectReadWithoutList exposes bucket objects to the internet without authentication. Keep access_type at NoPublicAccess.
remediation_fix: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, move the resource into private subnets, and front it with a load balancer or API gateway if external access is required. Verify with `aws ec2 describe-security-groups`.

title: VCN security list with open ingress
description: oci_core_security_list with an ingress_security_rules entry sourcing 0.0.0.0/0 permits traffic from the entire internet into the subnet. Restrict ingress sources to known CIDRs.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: IAM policy with wildcard manage permissions
description: oci_identity_policy with a statement like "Allow group ... to manage all-resources in tenancy" grants full administrative power over every resource, violating least privilege. Scope statements to the resource types and compartments the group needs.
remediation_fix: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

title: Block volume without KMS encryption
description: oci_core_volume without kms_key_id relies on Oracle-managed keys. Boot volumes and data volumes are block volumes: assign a customer-managed Vault key so you control encryption and revocation.
remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: Autonomous Database without customer-managed encryption
description: oci_database_autonomous_database without kms_key_id relies on Oracle-managed encryption. Assign a customer-managed Vault key for control over key rotation and revocation.
remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: Cloud Guard not enabled
description: oci_cloud_guard_cloud_guard_configuration without status = "ENABLED" leaves the tenancy without Cloud Guard threat detection and responder rules. Enable Cloud Guard with a reporting region.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Logging log with short retention
description: oci_logging_log with retention_period absent (provider default 30 days) or below 90 days discards audit and service logs before investigations finish. Retain logs at least 90 days.
remediation_fix: Enable audit logging. Turn on CloudTrail (multi-region, log file validation, KMS-encrypted bucket), VPC flow logs, and service access logs. Ship logs to a dedicated, MFA-delete-protected bucket in a security account.

title: Provider version affected by known advisory
description: A pinned Terraform provider version falls inside the affected range of a loaded supply-chain advisory (e.g. a CVE). Upgrade the provider beyond the affected range. Range constraints that are not concrete versions are not evaluated: the scanner cannot decide whether they resolve to a vulnerable version.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Lambda function uses a public ECR image
description: An aws_lambda_function with package_type=Image pulls its container image from public ECR (public.ecr.aws). Public images can be replaced or typosquatted; pin images by digest and prefer private repositories. Unknown or unresolved image URIs yield no finding.
remediation_fix: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, move the resource into private subnets, and front it with a load balancer or API gateway if external access is required. Verify with `aws ec2 describe-security-groups`.

title: user_data pipes a remote download into a shell
description: user_data containing 'curl ... | bash' or 'wget ... | sh' executes arbitrary remote code at instance launch with no integrity check. Vendor the script, verify a checksum or signature, or use a configuration management system instead. Unknown user_data yields no finding.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: EC2 instance uses an unpinned AMI
description: The ami attribute references a floating tag (contains "latest"). Floating AMI references make launches non-reproducible and let an attacker who compromises the AMI pipeline inject code into future instances. Pin AMIs by ID (ami-...). Variable or data-source references are unresolved and yield no finding.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Provisioner executes remote commands
description: A provisioner block with an 'inline' command list executes arbitrary commands on the remote host during apply (the remote-exec pattern). Provisioners are a last resort: they run outside the declarative model, often with elevated privileges, and their failures leave infrastructure half-configured. Prefer user_data, configuration management, or immutable images.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: null_resource executes local commands
description: A null_resource with a local-exec provisioner runs arbitrary commands on the machine executing Terraform. This is a common exfiltration and persistence vector in supply-chain attacks: a compromised module can steal credentials or implant backdoors on the operator's workstation or CI runner. Avoid null_resource provisioners entirely.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: External data source executes an arbitrary program
description: A data "external" block runs an arbitrary program during plan and apply, on the operator's machine, with the operator's credentials in the environment. A compromised module can use this to exfiltrate secrets or establish persistence. Avoid data "external"; prefer native data sources.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: user_data downloads over plain HTTP
description: user_data contains an http:// URL. Plain-HTTP downloads are vulnerable to man-in-the-middle tampering: an attacker on the network path can substitute a malicious payload that the instance then executes at boot. Use https:// URLs and verify checksums. Unknown user_data yields no finding.
remediation_fix: Enforce TLS 1.2+. Replace HTTP listeners with HTTPS, set a modern TLS policy (e.g. `ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06`), and redirect HTTP→HTTPS. Disable weak ciphers and old protocol versions everywhere.

title: Lambda function uses a layer from an unrecognized account
description: An aws_lambda_function references a Lambda layer published by an account outside the trusted publisher list. Third-party layers run with the function's privileges; a compromised or typosquatted layer is a direct code-execution vector. Vet the publisher and pin the layer version. Unresolvable layer lists yield no finding.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Terraform S3 backend without state encryption
description: The S3 backend stores the entire state file — including secrets — in the bucket. The encrypt argument defaults to false, so an S3 backend without encrypt = true keeps state in plaintext at rest.
remediation_fix: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

title: Terraform S3 backend without state locking
description: Without a DynamoDB lock table, concurrent Terraform runs can corrupt the state file. An S3 backend without dynamodb_table has no state locking.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Terraform provider without pinned version
description: A required_providers entry without a version constraint — or with an open-ended constraint like ">= 1.0" — lets a future provider release silently change plan/apply behavior, including security-relevant defaults.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Terraform CLI version not pinned
description: Without terraform.required_version, any CLI version may run this configuration; behavior and provider-protocol differences across versions can change what gets applied.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Terraform backend using plaintext HTTP
description: A backend address over http:// sends the state file — including secrets — in cleartext on the network.
remediation_fix: Enforce TLS 1.2+. Replace HTTP listeners with HTTPS, set a modern TLS policy (e.g. `ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06`), and redirect HTTP→HTTPS. Disable weak ciphers and old protocol versions everywhere.

title: Terraform local backend stores state in plaintext
description: The local backend keeps terraform.tfstate on disk unencrypted. State files contain secrets in cleartext; a remote encrypted backend should be used instead.
remediation_fix: Enforce TLS 1.2+. Replace HTTP listeners with HTTPS, set a modern TLS policy (e.g. `ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06`), and redirect HTTP→HTTPS. Disable weak ciphers and old protocol versions everywhere.

title: Terraform configuration without required_providers
description: Without a required_providers block, provider sources and versions are implicit; Terraform may select unexpected providers or versions.
remediation_fix: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

title: Terraform provider skips credentials validation
description: skip_credentials_validation = true disables the provider's startup credential checks, hiding misconfigured or expired credentials until apply time — or masking use of unintended accounts.
remediation_fix: Remove the hardcoded secret immediately and rotate it. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store (SecureString) and reference them via data sources. Never commit secrets to version control — scan history with gitleaks if the value was ever committed.
